## How Shopify interviews

Shopify's engineering loop pairs an hour-long conversation about your life with a long pair-programming session, and the company publishes its own description of how each round works. This guide goes beyond the outline on the company page, but be clear about its footing: it draws on 14 real Shopify questions and 0 candidate interview reports. Everything below about the loop comes from Shopify's public description of its process and from the question bank, not from first-hand candidate accounts, so treat round shapes and timings as typical rather than guaranteed.

### Interview Process

<!-- guide-diagram -->
![Shopify interview process — the rounds in order](https://cgppcnnkwbfiieexbrea.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/guides/shopify/process.webp)
<!-- guide-diagram -->

The stages below follow Shopify's public description of its process; the order and exact mix vary by team and level.

**Recruiter contact and the Life Story.** After an initial recruiter conversation about background and logistics, the first substantive round is typically the Life Story: a conversational interview, usually run by a recruiter rather than an engineer, that walks through your personal and professional history in roughly chronological order. Shopify has said it lasts about an hour and is used to read for impact, readiness, trust, engagement, and self-awareness. The company presents it as a genuine gate, and its own advice is to come as you are and reflect on the experiences that shaped your path rather than reciting a resume.

**Coding exercise.** A shorter live session, described publicly as around 40 minutes in a shared editor with a developer, in the language of your choice. It is pitched at algorithmic thinking and problem-solving approach. Shopify's own guidance is to ask clarifying questions before writing anything and to run the code often, debugging iteratively instead of chasing a perfect first draft. The question bank for this stage leans toward simulation and game-logic problems (robots on a grid, guess-the-number, word-guessing) rather than heavy data-structure puzzles.

**Pair programming.** The signature technical round: a longer session, described publicly as 75 to 90 minutes, where you write code while a Shopify developer collaborates, asks questions, and adds requirements. Language is your choice except that front-end roles are expected to use HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. More recent public descriptions of this round say candidates may work in their own IDE and use AI assistants, which shifts the grading toward how you direct the tool, whether you review and test what it produces, and how you communicate while doing it. Shopify states the evaluation criteria as communication, approach, edge-case handling, and code quality, and explicitly says a thoughtful incomplete solution beats a careless finished one.

**Technical deep dive.** A conversation, described publicly as about an hour, about previous projects you know thoroughly: business impact, architecture, technical decisions, trade-offs, what went wrong, and what you learned. Shopify advises picking projects of meaningful scope rather than solo side projects, and treating the round as a dialogue rather than a presentation.
